page: Microsoft Azure D32s_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an Intel Xeon Platinum 8272CL processor operating at a base frequency of 2.6 GHz. It provides 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading (2 threads per core) and dedicated CPU allocation. Memory capacity totals 128.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio (4.0 GB per vCPU). The processor includes 35 MB of L3 cache alongside support for AVX-512 vector extensions, including AVX-512 VNNI instructions.

The D32s_v4 instance does not provision integrated local disk storage or hardware accelerators, featuring zero local storage capacity and no GPUs. Persistent storage requires attachment to external Azure managed disks, with support for Premium Storage. This diskless configuration means the instance relies entirely on network-attached storage architectures, avoiding ephemeral drive management while requiring careful IOPS and throughput planning via remote volumes.

Benchmark results place the D32s_v4 primarily within the middle tier for compute and data processing tasks. The instance achieved an average stress-ng multi-core score of 29831.05 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 10997.0. Memory subsystem testing demonstrated strong results, with a PassMark memory score of 2845.98 placing in the top quartile, supported by large-block read bandwidth of 108.56 GB/sec. Application testing yielded 26.08 million operations per second on Redis SET workloads and 20.31 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. CPU-based small LLM inference achieves viable throughput, though larger models exhibit severe performance drop-offs. The profile is suited for general enterprise applications, mid-sized relational and in-memory databases, continuous integration build clusters, and high-concurrency web tiers.

Configured with 32 dedicated vCPUs (16 physical cores with hyperthreading) and 128.0 GB of system memory, the instance maintains a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. It does not include bundled local storage or GPU accelerators, relying instead on network-attached remote storage with Premium Storage support. Benchmark data reflects consistent middle-tier compute output, highlighted by a multi-core Geekbench score of 10997.0 and a multi-core stress-ng rating of 29831.05. Memory subsystem performance is strong, registering in the top 25 percent on PassMark memory benchmarks with 108.56 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth. Workload processing delivers 26.08 million Redis SET operations per second and 20.31 GB/sec web serving throughput, making this server suitable for enterprise web serving, backend application runtimes, in-memory caching systems, and build automation.
